answer: Think of trust as a terrace garden: each identity starts on the lowest terrace with almost no weight, and climbs only by earning capability tokens that expire unless unrelated peers renew them. A lone attacker wandering the tundra of empty accounts finds no oasis: fresh attestations must come from strangers with no shared funding trail, and every renewal costs real useful work. Cloning accounts multiplies the work instead of the reward, so sybils wither while honest agents climb.
